Article Title: After recent PG doctor suicide, NMC seeks report on harassment allegations at Indore medical college
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Weeks after the alleged suicide of a postgraduate medical student in Surat triggered fresh concerns over harassment and ragging in medical colleges, the National Medical Commission (NMC) has sought a para-wise report within 24 hours from MGM Medical College and MY Hospital, Indore, on allegations of mental harassment, public humiliation and academic intimidation of a first-year postgraduate resident.The complaint concerns Dr Simmi Yadav, a first-year postgraduate resident in the Department of Obstetrics & Gynaecology. Filed by her brother, it alleges that she attempted suicide by insulin overdose and is currently in the intensive care unit.The case comes amid continuing concerns over the treatment of junior doctors and medical students. In a December 2024 advisory, the NMC said it continued to receive numerous complaints involving undergraduate and postgraduate students, including cases of mental harassment and instances leading to suicide.The complaint alleges that Dr Simmi was repeatedly humiliated over minor mistakes, threatened with adverse academic consequences and made to undertake non-academic work. The NMC has directed the college to examine the allegations against the concerned residents and faculty and furnish their responses.The commission has sought her duty rosters, attendance and biometric records, handover registers and leave records to verify allegations that she was working 14-15 hours despite an official roster showing around 12-hour duties.It has also ordered confidential interactions with other PG residents to ascertain whether similar instances of harassment, intimidation or coercion have been reported. The college has been asked to preserve WhatsApp messages, emails, complaints, duty and academic records and other evidence.The NMC has further sought details of the functioning of the college's Anti-Ragging Committee and Squad, counselling and mental-health support available to PG residents, and compliance with anti-ragging regulations.The regulator's own National Task Force on the mental health of medical students found that 26.7% of respondents reported harassment by senior postgraduate students in clinical settings, highlighting concerns about the working environment faced by junior doctors.The commission has directed the college to ensure that Dr Simmi does not face retaliation, victimisation or adverse academic treatment for raising the complaint or participating in the inquiry. The Action Taken Report, supported by documents, has to be submitted within 24 hours.
Article Summary: The complaint concerns dr simmi yadav, a first-year postgraduate resident in the department of obstetrics & gynaecology. Filed by her brother, it alleges that she attempted suicide by insulin overdose and is currently in the intensive care unit. The case comes amid continuing concerns over the treatment of junior doctors and medical students.

Article Title: ‘Few actors possessed his intensity’: PM Modi mourns Nana Patekar
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday condoled veteran actor Nana Patekar , remembering his “immense” contribution to Hindi and Marathi cinema and praising his versatility and creativity.In a post on X, PM Modi wrote: “Few actors possessed the intensity, individuality and unmistakable presence that Shri Nana Patekar Ji had. He brought remarkable versatility and creativity to every role and gave us characters that will be remembered for generations. He was also admired for his frank and forthright views, never hesitating to express what he believed in.”He added: “Shri Nana Patekar’s contribution to Hindi and Marathi cinema was immense. His passing leaves a deep void. My condolences to his family, friends and countless admirers. Om Shanti.”While speaking at an event in Delhi, PM Modi remembered veteran actor.“This morning we got the news that the renowned actor Nana Patekar is no longer with us. He was an exceptional artist who won the hearts of audiences through a variety of roles,” PM Modi said.The Prime Minister said Patekar’s life was dedicated to the “honour and glory of the Tricolour” and used references to some of the actor’s well-known films to describe his career.“Nana Patekar’s life was dedicated to the honour and glory of the Tricolour. He refused to be bound by constraints; like a ‘Parinda’, he soared through the vast skies of cinema,” PM Modi said.He said Patekar used his films to raise questions about social issues and challenge the prevailing order.“Through his films, he launched scathing attacks on the prevailing societal order. He was a true Krantiveer who fought against social evils,” PM Modi said.PM also recalled Patekar’s distinctive screen presence, saying, “His silence was as impactful as his speech was powerful.”The Prime Minister said Patekar consistently spoke against anti-national elements and paid tribute to the actor while offering condolences to his family and admirers.“I pay tribute to Nana Patekar and offer my condolences to his family and admirers,” PM Modi said.Meanwhile, Union home minister Amit Shah also mourned Patekar, sharing a picture with the veteran actor and calling his passing an “irreparable loss” to the world of art.In a post, Shah wrote: “Over five decades, with his natural acting and powerful dialogue delivery, he left an indelible mark on the hearts of audiences. Whether it was serious social issues or humor-satire, he brought to life every character he portrayed. Through the 'Naam Foundation,' serving drought-stricken farmer families, or going to the border to boost the morale of soldiers, even after reaching the pinnacle of fame, he remained connected to his roots. ”He added: “Whenever I met him, his simplicity and straightforwardness always left a deep impression. May God grant strength to the grieving family and fans to bear this sorrow, and may the departed soul find a place at His divine feet.”Defence minister Rajnath Singh also paid tribute to Patekar, writing: “Nana Patekar was not merely an actor; he was an institution in himself. His remarkable contribution to Indian cinema will continue to inspire generations.”Patekar suffered a cardiac arrest at his home in Goa and was found unconscious. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead.Known for films including Prahaar, Parinda, Krantiveer, Tirangaa and Welcome, Patekar was one of the most recognised actors in Hindi and Marathi cinema.
Article Summary: Nana patekar dies: pm modi mourns veteran actor, hails ‘immense’ contribution to cinema. Pm modi: “few actors possessed the intensity, individuality and unmistakable presence’ union home minister amit shah calls his passing an ‘irreparable loss’ to the world of art.

Article Title: Congress protest: Delhi Police to scan videos to identify protesters accused of assaulting personnel; FIR likely

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police is examining several mobile phone videos to identify protesters allegedly involved in the assault and obstruction of police personnel during a Congress protest near Jantar Mantar, police sources said on Thursday.The footage, including videos showing women police officers and constables allegedly being assaulted, is being analysed to establish the sequence of events and identify those involved, the sources said, as cited by news agency PTI.The police are also examining footage from other sources to identify people who allegedly manhandled or obstructed personnel deployed to maintain law and order during the protest.Delhi Police is likely to register an FIR under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to assault on public servants, obstructing public servants in the discharge of their duties and other applicable sections, the sources said.The investigation comes after Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi , along with their supporters, staged protests on Tuesday and Wednesday over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Around 90 people, including Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi, were detained by Delhi Police on Wednesday after they were stopped from proceeding towards Jantar Mantar.Both leaders were later released from police detention a little after 8 pm.Rahul Gandhi was taken to Barakhamba police station, while Priyanka Gandhi was taken to Chhatrasal Stadium, officials said.The latest video examination is also taking place amid police action over social media posts related to the protests.The Delhi Police had asked a social media platform to remove or restrict access to 11 posts and videos that it alleged presented a misleading account of police action during a recent protest.In notices issued under the Information Technology Act, the police alleged that some protesters had pushed against personnel, removed or jumped over barricades and attempted to proceed despite restrictions imposed under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).The police said personnel subsequently restrained or detained some protesters while discharging their duties.According to the notice, some videos “appear to be selectively” portraying the subsequent police intervention as “misbehaviour or unwarranted use of force”, while allegedly leaving out the preceding acts of obstruction, resistance and non-compliance.The police described the portrayal as “selective, misleading and contextually incomplete” and said it could create a false narrative about the conduct of its personnel, provoke public reaction and undermine confidence in law-and-order measures.Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi were among opposition leaders and Congress workers who travelled towards Jantar Mantar on Wednesday, but police stopped them from proceeding further.The protesters then staged a sit-in near a roundabout close to the Shangri-La hotel in central Delhi.Priyanka Gandhi and several women leaders lay on the road while carrying a copy of the Constitution. Security personnel subsequently removed the protesters from the spot.“This is how they treat members of Parliament who are asking simply to meet the election commissioners. This is how they treat us. They are beating members of Parliament,” Priyanka Gandhi said.The detentions came a day after Delhi Police registered an FIR against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and their supporters over allegations that they forcibly entered Akashvani Bhawan during a protest on October 6.Police said the FIR followed a complaint alleging that the two Congress leaders, their supporters and other MPs entered the premises without permission.Medico-legal examinations were also conducted on two security guards who allegedly sustained injuries when protesters tried to enter the building.On Tuesday, Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi were among around 260 people detained after an over eight-hour sit-in inside Akashvani Bhawan following an opposition march towards the Election Commission office.Delhi Police had said no application seeking permission for the march had been submitted to the Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, and no permission had been granted.
Article Summary: Delhi police likely to file fir over alleged assault on police during protest. Police examining social media videos about congress protests over electoral roll revision. Around 90 people, including rahul and priyanka gandhi, were detained by delhi police on wednesday after they were stopped from proceeding towards jantar mantar.

NEW DELHI: Punishment and compassion may not mix in the justice delivery process, but they probably can walk together. Adopting this approach, Supreme Court Wednesday refused to relax the pre-condition of depositing Rs 2 crore for hearing the appeal of comedian Rajpal Yadav challenging his conviction and sentence of three months in a cheque bouncing case but suggested that he make a good film that would enable him to repay debts.A loan of Rs 5 crore he had taken in 2010 for producing the film 'Aata Pata Lapata', which remained on the verge of completion and never released because of litigation, spiralled into a huge sum with interest.A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalaya Bagchi and V Mohana assured senior advocate Ajit Kumar Sinha, who appeared for Muli Projects that had advanced the loan to Yadav, that it would ensure that the loan is repaid.Yadav was to deposit Rs 2 crore as a pre-condition for hearing of his appeal by Wednesday.Yadav's counsel Vikrant Yadav told the court that he has got a demand draft for Rs 1.15 crore and he has entered into an agreement with one Anand Prakash Yadav, who also was present in the court, to sell off his property. He sought time till Oct 13 to deposit the balance amount of Rs 85 lakh. SC agreed and protected him from surrendering to undergo jail term.The CJI said, "Make a good film and entertain people. You will be able to repay the loans." The apex court posted the case for hearing on Oct 15.

Article Title: From 'vote chori' to 'chita andolan': Street protests return with a new playbook
Article Text:
Street protests are back, this time with new tools

During the INDIA bloc’s protest against the CEC, Priyanka Gandhi lay down on the road, daring anyone to move her.

The street has always been a political stage

How social media changed street mobilisation

Protest against CEC over SIR process in Delhi

When the youth lead, parties follow

Rahul Gandhi being taken away by police during a Congress protest against police action on demonstrators at Jantar Mantar.

Beyond Jantar Mantar: The protests away from the spotlight

Protest on women's sa​fety in Delhi

Protesters stage the 'Chita Andolan' in Madhya Pradesh's Panna district, demanding compensation and rehabilitation.

The street is old, the tools are changing

NEW DELHI: Slogans are ringing out, crowds are turning up and the streets are once again abuzz with protests.On Tuesday, INDIA bloc MPs took their protest against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to the national capital, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The march took an unexpected turn when Rahul Gandhi surprised the police with a last-minute change of course, turning it into a sit-in.A day later, opposition MPs were back with another dramatic flash protest on Janpath streets, where Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay down on the road and refused to budge until the CEC agreed to meet opposition leaders.And more could be coming. Cockroach Janata Party’s Abhijeet Dipke, who rallied young protesters during the anti-NEET paper leak agitation in July, has warned of a “Jantar Mantar 2.0” on October 10 if the CEC does not resign.But Delhi is not the only place, and politicians are not the only ones taking their grievances to the streets. Across the country, protests over very different issues are bringing people out in an attempt to make their voices heard.The protests differ in scale, issue and leadership. But together, they point to something familiar returning to the foreground: street politics.Peaceful protests have always been a part of our democracy.India's politics has rarely been confined to Parliament, party offices or election rallies. The streets have always had a part to play.Mahatma Gandhi turned marches, boycotts and satyagraha into instruments of mass politics during the freedom struggle. Decades later, Jayaprakash Narayan's movement drew students and citizens onto the streets against the Indira Gandhi government.Anna Hazare's anti-corruption protests filled Jantar Mantar and Ramlila Maidan in 2011. The anti-CAA protests saw prolonged sit-ins, while farmers camped at Delhi's borders for more than a year before the three farm laws were repealed.Street politics, then, is hardly new. What keeps changing are the tools used to trigger, spread and sustain mobilisation. Political analyst Uday Chandra feels social media is making protests more visible while also changing who can start and sustain them."Social media certainly makes protests visible to millions, enabling a rapid or viral spread. But it also does something more important: it reduces dependence on political parties, unions and established organisations to mobilise people. A grievance may now turn into a movement before conventional political actors decide how to respond," Uday Chandra says.But the current round of protests goes beyond social-media amplification, feels Chandra."I think something real is happening beyond social-media amplification. Street protest never quite disappeared from politics in India, but for much of the past decade, electoral politics under a highly centralised party machinery overshadowed it. What we are seeing now is, to my mind, the re-emergence of the street as an autonomous political arena," he said.What stands out in this round of protests is not just the issues being raised, but who is often raising them first.On questions ranging from examinations to electoral rolls, young people have managed to create pressure outside the usual party machinery. Increasingly, political parties have found themselves responding aggressively to issues they did not start.So, have young people and students shown political parties the way back to street mobilisation? The events surrounding the NEET protests in July this year are a case in point.As students protested over the paper leak, Jantar Mantar became the centre of an agitation that continued for weeks. The CJP emerged as the pressure group leading the agitation and eventually ensuring the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.Many political parties that initially stood on the sidelines scrambled to join the agitation. On July 21, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Mallikarjun Kharge and other opposition leaders staged a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence over police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak.But Chandra argues that the CJP, as a movement, differs significantly from political parties and earlier large movements such as the Anna Hazare agitation or the farmers' protests."CJP is much more decentralised than the two movements you mention. The Anna movement had recognisable leaders and a national campaign/agenda. Likewise, the farmers’ protests rested on strong unions, local organisation, and the economic capacity to sustain mobilisation for months. By contrast, what we see emerging now is networked, relatively leader-light, and often issue-specific," he said.The CJP advantage is also organisational, he feels."Instagram, WhatsApp, YouTube and other online platforms can connect previously unrelated groups rapidly. Mobilisation is, therefore, not only faster but more fluid. You do not necessarily need to build and register an organisation before launching a movement. Increasingly, the movement precedes the organisation," Chandra adds.It is perhaps this realisation that has forced political parties to course-correct their mobilisation strategies.Rahul Gandhi, who faced criticism for prioritising his "Chhatron ki Goonj" campaign instead of backing the anti-NEET protests led by CJP, has now made a more direct attempt to help Congress enter the protest space. On October 4, he launched the 'Satyagraha' portal, which seeks to map protests across the country and connect people agitating over different issues.For Chandra, the move shows that Congress has recognised the risks of ignoring protests that begin online and then spill onto the streets."The Satyagraha platform strikes me as an attempt to situate the INC within an emerging ecology of anti-BJP protests. This is an interesting shift in political organisation. It takes the party from a traditional top-heavy high command structure to a node connecting diverse and dispersed struggles against the status quo."The high-decibel protests against Gyanesh Kumar or over NEET are only one part of the story, perhaps the more visible one. Away from the national spotlight, peaceful protests have been taking place across the country over a wide range of issues.They may be small, localised and often unconnected: women’s safety, land, displacement, water, facilities in schools, local governance and more. But together, they show how the street remains an important space for people trying to make themselves heard.In Delhi, young women have marched over women's safety after cases of sexual violence. Demonstrations have also spread to cities including Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Ahmedabad, Patna and Dehradun, with protesters demanding safer public spaces and greater accountability from governments and police.In Madhya Pradesh’s Panna district, families affected by the Ken-Betwa river-linking project have revived their "Chita Andolan". Protesters have slept on funeral pyres, stood in water and gone on hunger strike over compensation and rehabilitation.In Maharashtra’s Maval, farmers opposing the Pavana closed pipeline project announced a 'jal samadhi' agitation while also demanding rehabilitation for families that surrendered land for the Pavana dam decades ago.Water has also brought farmers onto the streets in Karnataka, where organisations in Krishna basin districts have opposed releasing reservoir water to Telangana, arguing that drought-hit areas within Karnataka should be given priority.At IIT Bombay too, students have turned their protest over the death by suicide of student Sahil Wakode into a hunger strike, with the JNU Students’ Union joining calls for action on the demands raised by protesters.The scale and demands vary sharply. Some protests involve thousands; others are confined to a university campus, a few villages or even a handful of streets. They may target the Centre, state governments, local administrations or institutions, but the impulse is the same: take the grievance to the street.So, street politics is old, but the mobilisation techniques have changed. Earlier movements depended heavily on student organisations, unions, public meetings and, later, television coverage. Today, a protest can begin on Instagram or X before it reaches Jantar Mantar.Social media has also changed the language of protest. A slogan shouted on the street can become a meme within hours, while posters, one-liners, chants and songs travel far beyond the protest site.Recent demonstrations have offered plenty of examples. At women's protests in Delhi, slogans such as 'Ek kachori, do samosa, in mardon ka kya bharosa' quickly travelled from the street to Instagram reels, using humour and rhyme to make a serious point about women's safety and gender attitudes.At the Mumbai protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, placards carried lines such as 'Gyanu must go' and the Bollywood-inspired 'Vote churaya mera, kisne o sanam? Gyanu ne'. Days later, Rahul Gandhi carried the Gen Z-style message "Gyanesh, it's done bro!" during the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission. Whether it will culiminate into effective but what it definitely did was make people stop and notice.And Gen Z may not be the youngest generation learning to protest.In Lucknow, around 200 schoolgirls blocked a road in the rain over a shortage of teachers and a damaged road leading to their school. In Fatehpur, around 1,000 students staged a four-hour protest demanding drinking water and repairs to classrooms. In several cases, authorities acted after the protests.What has changed is not the instinct to protest, but how quickly a grievance can find an audience and become visible. The slogan may now become a meme and the mobilisation may begin on a phone screen. The destination, however, is often still the same: the street.
Article Summary: Street protests are back, this time with new tools to trigger, spread and sustain mobilisation. Political analyst uday chandra feels social media is making protests more visible. But the current round of protests goes beyond social-media amplification, feels chandra.

Article Title: India’s first high-altitude snow leopard safari flagged off in Ladakh
Article Text:
File photo: Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena

LEH/JAMMU: Ladakh lieutenant governor, Vinai Kumar Saxena, Wednesday flagged off India’s first high-altitude wildlife safari focused on snow leopard trails, with an aim of making local communities “equal partners in protecting and promoting Ladakh’s wildlife and benefiting economically”.“Wildlife should not be protected at the cost of people, nor should development come at the cost of wildlife. We must create a model in which both can thrive together,” the LG said after flagging off six safari vehicles.The project, operated by the Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation (SHAN) Society in collaboration with the UT’s forest department, has mapped the safari routes through Hemis National Park, Changthang and Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary, besides Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil, and Drass districts.Ladakh has 477 snow leopards out of 477 across India. The region is also home to more than 38 mammal species, over 340 bird species, and around 1,800 vascular plant species.

NEW DELHI: The President, world leaders and BJP-led NDA members Wednesday congratulated PM Narendra Modi on his 25-year unbroken stint as head of govt, with President Droupadi Murmu saying the momentous milestone reflected his steadfast commitment to people's well-being and India's progress."The transformation witnessed across our country in recent years is visible in the lives of people," she said.Home minister Amit Shah said Modi's journey of service, struggle and dedication since 2001 was synonymous with the welfare of the poor, women's empowerment and prosperity of every section of society. Recalling his meeting in New Delhi in 2019 as a private citizen, Tobgay said he told the PM he saw him as an elder brother and "an avatar of Vishnu"."In our part of the world, I explained, enlightened rulers have long been regarded as such," Tobgay said, adding Modi awakened in Indians a "powerful belief in themselves and in their country".Belgium's PM Bart De Wever, Dominican PM Roosevelt Skerrit and Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu sent congratulatory messages and praised Modi's leadership.

Article Title: Supreme Court to study plea for recall of split verdict on EC appointment law
Article Text:
File photo

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its recent split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the chief election commissioner and election commissioners should be referred to a larger Constitution bench.On Sept 23, a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma gave split opinions on whether a batch of pleas challenging the validity of a 2023 law that excludes the CJI from the selection panel should go to a Constitution bench.Justice Datta declined the Centre's request for such a reference, while Justice Sharma favoured placing the matter before a larger bench.It had said due to a difference of opinion, the matter would be placed before CJI Surya Kant on the administrative side for the constitution of a bench of appropriate strength for an effective and authoritative adjudication.On Wednesday, a bench comprising the CJI and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told about the recall application by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan. "We will examine and take a call," the CJI said.Sankaranarayanan told the bench that the recall application had earlier been mentioned before a bench headed by Justice Datta, but the matter had been released and he was asked to mention it before the CJI.When the CJI asked whether there was any other interlocutory application, Sankaranarayanan said a curative petition had also been filed. "That, I think, will have to go in its own form," he said.The petitions had challenged the constitutional validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which replaced the selection mechanism laid down by SC in its March 2, 2023 judgement.In that ruling, a five-judge Constitution bench had directed that the CEC and ECs be appointed by the President on the advice of a committee comprising the PM, the leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha and the CJI. Parliament subsequently enacted the 2023 law, under which the selection committee comprises the PM, a Un-ion Cabinet minister nominated by the PM and the leader of the opposition in LS.
Article Summary: Supreme court agrees to examine a plea seeking recall of its recent split verdict. Justices dipankar datta and satish chandra sharma gave split opinions on whether a batch of pleas challenging the validity of a 2023 law that excludes the cji from the selection panel should go to a constitution bench.

Article Title: Centre cites Supreme Court order, seeks to void Jharkhand DGP appointment
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to hear an application by Centre seeking the annulment of the appointment of Tadasha Mishra as Jharkhand DGP on the ground that it was in violation of procedures laid down in SC's 2006 Prakash Singh judgement.Arguing that the appointments of the last two DGPs were also illegal, Centre said Mishra was appointed the state's police chief just a day before she was to retire, which was in conflict with the SC order that disapproved the practice among states to appoint DGPs on the last date of their tenure so that the person remained in the crucial position for two more years.SC had also clarified that the officers who are empanelled by the state, as far as practicable, must have two years of service left. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said though an application on the matter was filed more than a month ago, it had not yet been listed for hearing. A bench headed by CJI Surya Kant directed it to be listed for Thursday.Centre questioned the legality of Jharkhand's 'Selection and Appointment of DGP (Head of Police Force) Regulation, 2025 and said the regulations are ex-facie violative of various SC directives, especially its ruling that a state could pick DGP from among those on a panel prepared by UPSC.A petition challenging the validity of the 2025 regulations was transferred from Jharkhand HC to SC in Aug last year. Jharkhand govt appointed Mishra as DGP on Dec 30 last year after amending its own 2025 regulations, which too mandated six months residual service prior to superannuation. MHA had written to Jharkhand to cancel the appointment and take steps to appoint a new DGP.
Article Summary: Supreme court agrees to hear application by centre seeking annulment of tadasha mishra's appointment as jharkhand dgp. Centre says appointment was in violation of procedures laid down in sc's 2006 prakash singh judgement. Centre said mishra was appointed the state's police chief just a day before she was to retire, which was in conflict with sc order.

One of these policies pertains to "foodgrain labour and cartage", which was allegedly shared by Gohal with co-accused Nagra, who has a foodgrain supply business.Nagra is accused of asking for favourable changes in the policy through Gohal, per the FIR.CBI has also obtained other purportedly incriminating documents about real estate projects, cooperative housing and irregularities in the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority, suggesting interference by "multiple private individuals" in govt functioning. CBI's probe focuses on allegations of corruption by influencing transfers, including those of IAS and IPS officers, matters pertaining to policy formulation, tender conditions, revenue and land-related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefits.

Article Title: Medical trips costliest in both rural & urban areas
Article Text:
Representative image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Health and medical trips were most expensive among all trips completed in a year with average expenditure of Rs 29,454 in rural areas and Rs 41,649 in urban areas. Of this expenditure, over 70% was spent on medical treatment. The largest chunk of travel (48.7%) in a year was for pilgrimage or religious purposes.This was revealed in the survey on Domestic Tourism Expenditure conducted from July 2025 to June 2026 as part of National Sample Survey's 80th round. The survey collected information on purpose and expenditure of domestic travel, including overnight trips, and same-day journeys, and categories of expenditure during the trips.The report showed that of the expenditure on travel for health and medical needs, 10% was for accommodation, followed by 5% each for food and drink and transport. For two other major categories of travel - holidaying, leisure and recreation, and for pilgrimage and recreation - transport was the largest chunk of expenditure. In case of overnight trips for shopping, the biggest chunk of expenditure was not surprisingly on shopping.Rented or hired transport was the most popular for medical and health-centred trips accounting for almost 47% of trips in rural areas and about 40% in urban areas, followed by buses - 26% in rural areas and 21% in urban. Those surveyed used their own vehicle in less than a quarter of these trips in urban areas and less than one in five in rural.Average expenditure per same-day trip, incurred by households in rural and urban areas, was highest for trips undertaken for 'shopping' (Rs 1,795 for rural, Rs 2,631 for urban) and 'health and medical' accounted for the second costliest purpose (Rs 1,499 for rural, Rs 1,859 for urban). For same-day trips, travel for health and medical needs figured after travel for social purpose and shopping.
Article Summary: Health and medical trips were most expensive among all trips completed in a year with average expenditure of rs 29,454 in rural areas and rs 41,649 in urban areas. Of this expenditure, over 70% was spent on medical treatment. The largest chunk of travel (48.7%) was for pilgrimage or religious purposes.

NEW DELHI: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma's claim that Mumtaz Begum, a 43-year-old woman who was sent to Bangladesh in June, is safe and in daily touch with her son has left her family with questions.Her son, Momruz Ali (26), told TOI Wednesday that he has had no contact with his mother and received no official communication from authorities about her whereabouts. "The CM says he knows she is safe... but we have no way to find out," he said. "We are just an ordinary family with little means. How will we ever find her?"Ali's plea to the Assam and Indian govts is simple: find his mother - "in Assam, India or Bangladesh". If she is alive, he said, "she has to be on either side". "It's govt's job. Assam Police must take responsibility for finding her," he said.The family's anguish is sharpened by Sarma's earlier remarks that people pushed across the border can cross back into India. "The CM, in a press conference two years ago, said that people cross over and return. In that case, they should search in Assam also. Why only Bangladesh?" Ali saidOn Sept 3, Gauhati HC directed the external affairs ministry to locate Mumtaz in Bangladesh and bring her back to pursue her case before the foreigners tribunal.It ordered Rs 2 lakh interim compensation for her husband, noting she had been expelled without an adult family member being informed.Declared a foreigner in 2019, Mumtaz had got relief from the HC in April this year, which set aside the tribunal's opinion and ordered fresh consideration of her case, citing deficiencies in its assessment of voter-list records and other citizenship documents. She appeared before the tribunal on May 30, was taken into custody and handed over to BSF before being sent to Bangladesh.TOI reported on Sept 29 that Bangladesh's home ministry had begun searching for Mumtaz after the newspaper reached out to authorities in that country. The matter was referred to relevant departments, but officials had no information. Searches in Sylhet have produced no breakthrough, with Sylhet Ran-ge DIG Mohammad Jahangir Hossain telling TOI he too was trying to locate her.
Article Summary: Mumtaz begum, 43, was sent to bangladesh in june. Her son says he has had no contact with his mother and received no official communication about her whereabouts. "the cm says he knows she is safe... but we have no way to find out," he said.

Article Title: 'One student, one day': CUET-UG 2027 may get shorter, simpler
Article Text:
File photo: Students at a CUET-UG centre

CUET-UG also mulls reducing number of subjects from 5 to 4

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: CUET-UG 2027 could see some of its biggest changes yet - fewer subjects, shorter papers and a new grouping system aimed at ensuring that a student can finish the entire entrance test in a single day instead of making repeated trips to examination centres.The ministry of education, University Grants Commission and National Testing Agency are working on a formula to shorten the overall examination cycle and simplify the experience for candidates, sources said.At present, a candidate can take up to five subjects in CUET-UG, with each paper lasting 60 minutes.Under one proposal being examined, the duration of individual papers could be reduced so that even a student taking five subjects can complete all tests within about 180 to 200 minutes.Another option under discussion is whether the maximum number of subjects should be reduced from five to four. Sources said senior officials of the education ministry , UGC and NTA recently discussed the proposed changes and asked officials to examine how the examination could be compressed without affecting university admission requirements.A key part of the plan is to create subject groups based on commonly chosen combinations.This would allow NTA to schedule related papers together and complete a candidate’s examination in one sitting or on the same day.For example, physics, chemistry and biology could form one group for those seeking admission to science programmes. General studies could be added as a fourth paper where universities give weightage to its score. The idea is to bu-ild these groups around eligibility rules followed by universities.For instance, a student seeking admission to physics (Hons) at DU could choose the relevant three-subject combination rather than taking papers not required for the course.Officials believe such grouping could reduce the number of examination days and make scheduling easier. It could also end the problem of students having to travel to examination centres on different days for different papers. The proposals will depend on consultations with universities and the testing agency.
Article Summary: The ministry of education, university grants commission and national testing agency are working on a formula to shorten the overall examination cycle. A key part of the plan is to create subject groups based on commonly chosen combinations. This would allow nta to schedule related papers together and complete a candidate’s examination in one sitting or on the same day.

Article Title: Anti-CEC protests: Opposition, police face off again; Rahul Gandhi says won’t stop till Gyanesh quits
Article Text:
TOI’s photographer took this photo of a sit-in at Windsor Place roundabout in central Delhi from atop a bus, which was driven away by police while he and others were still on the roof

My target is 100 FIRs against me. Every FIR a medal: Rahul

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Opposition INDIA bloc members on Wednesday travelled by buses from their lunch meeting in Connaught Place towards Jantar Mantar, seeking to protest and demand CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. But for the second day in a row, Delhi Police stalled their agitation, detaining them less than 1km from their intended “flash protest” site.“We are not going to stop protesting till CEC Gyanesh Kumar resigns,” said Rahul Gandhi , who was detained along with 90 others, including MPs and workers, after hours of confrontation with police in front of Shangri-La hotel. They were taken to Barakhamba police station and released later around 8:30 pm.Later, Congress issued a directive to all its state, block and district committees, to hold “massive demonstrations” to protest the police action to prevent the INDIA bloc from holding a protest at Jantar Mantar. “Congress declares today as a black day for Indian democracy,” it stated.The joint opposition made it clear that their protest will continue undeterred and a bigger protest plan is in the works for Thursday.However, Delhi Police said restrictions imposed under BNSS’s Section 163 were in force in the New Delhi area, which is why the protesters were detained. “As Section 163 is in force here… protest marches or demonstrations are not allowed without permission,” DCP Sachin Sharma said.It all began with Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge hosting INDIA bloc MPs for lunch at a restaurant in Janpath, which began around 1.30pm and where the gathering was informed about a plan to continue the protest against CEC, this time with a march to Jantar Mantar for a demonstration.Members, including Congress’s Rahul, KC Venugopal and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, John Brittas (CPM), P Sandosh Kumar (CPI), Manoj Jha (RJD), Derek O’Brien (TMC), Thol Thirumavalavan (VCK), emerged from the restaurant and announced the protest plan. MPs of JMM and IUML also joined them.They headed for buses waiting for them to leave. But the administration had stationed police in heavy numbers at Janpath, which, coupled with the gathering of onlookers and rush of political workers, made it difficult for the buses to move. Some Congress MPs and functionaries climbed on the roof of one of the buses, waving Tricolour. The MPs were forced to dismount from the buses in front of the hotel, where they were surrounded by police. Priyanka, Raja Warring and Deepender Hooda sat down on the road along with some workers, even as the cops continued to request Rahul to get into a bus. Cops finally picked up Rahul and took him away in a mini van. Similarly, Priyanka, who was lying on the street clutching a copy of the Constitution, along with other women workers of her party, was removed.Police claimed that some protesters attacked their personnel. A sub-inspector alleged protesters bit him and tore his uniform. Police are also analysing mobile-phone videos following allegations that police personnel, including women, were assaulted near Jantar Mantar.Kharge and Rahul said the opposition will continue with its protests till CEC resigns. On an FIR being registered against him for entering Akashvani Bhavan premises and staging an eight-hour sit-in Tuesday, Rahul said, “I have 45 FIRs against me. My target is that there should be 100 FIRs against me. Every FIR against me is a medal for me.” Rahul said the opposition decided to demonstrate at Jantar Mantar, which is the designated protest site, as govt told them that dharna couldn’t be held at places like Election Commission.While some of Congress’ allies were absent from the lunch, party spokesperson Jairam Ramesh said the decision for lunch was taken late Tuesday night, and the absence was understandable.On Samajwadi Party, O’Brien said there was a minor miscommunication, which was addressed swiftly, and Samajwadi Party will join the protest Thursday.Sources said Congress had reached out to certain opposition parties to make it clear there was some misunderstanding and the decision to enter Akashwani Bhavan Tuesday was taken on the spur. Left and TMC functionaries were also dismissive of any lingering differences.
Article Summary: Opposition india bloc members on wednesday travelled by buses from their lunch meeting in connaught place towards jantar mantar. But for the second day in a row, delhi police stalled their agitation, detaining them less than 1km from their intended ‘flash protest’ site.

Article Text:

JAMMU: A 19-year-old woman from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), whom the Army had detained along the Line of Control (LoC) in Rajouri’s Nowshera last week, was repatriated Wednesday through Chakkan Da Bagh in Poonch district.Army’s 6/1 Gorkha Rifles had apprehended the woman—Samiya Azeem from Bains Gala, Seri, in PoK’s Kotli district—in Lam area on Oct 2 after she entered India.
